transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-20 16:00 PT | Duration: ~42m | Recording: auto
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Sherwood - Sec Lead), Liam O'Connor (Sherwood - Platform), Hannah Lee (Sherwood - Legal)

[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you confirm names?
[00:03] Priya Rao (Sherwood): This is Priya, Priya Rao, security lead.
[00:05] Liam O'Connor (Sherwood): Liam here. Platform.
[00:06] Hannah Lee (Sherwood): Hannah from legal.
[00:08] Maya: Great. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Arjun is our SE. We wanted to focus on security posture today — SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, KMS, retention and audit logs. Does that align with what you wanted?
[00:16] Priya: Yes, definitely. We're starting an eval across hosted/dedicated/private and security is the gating factor.
[00:20] Arjun Patel (Redwood SE): Quick note — I might jump to a few architecture slides if useful, otherwise we can keep it Q&A.
[00:25] Hannah: That works. Priya will lead on requirements and I'll chime in on legal/contract needs.

[00:30] ----- Topics: SOC2 / ISO, SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, retention -----

[00:45] Priya: Our baseline — we need SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 or an equivalent attestation. For any production use we need proof of controls. Does Redwood have public attestation?
[00:54] Maya: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and an ISO summary; we can share the reports and a SOC2 matrix. It's standard for hosted, and for Dedicated/Private we provide architecture diagrams and controls mapping.
[01:02] Liam: For private deployments, are the controls the same or is there a shared responsibility model?
[01:07] Arjun: There's always shared responsibility. For Private (VPC or on-prem), Redwood provides the control plane and audit logging hooks; customer is responsible for network controls, key management if you choose customer-managed KMS, and some physical security on-prem. We can map each control on the matrix.
[01:18] Priya: Good. We want SSO — SAML with MFA enforced by our IdP. How is SSO integrated and can we enforce Azure AD conditional access?
[01:26] Maya: Yes — SAML 2.0 SSO with SCIM provisioning for user sync. You can enforce MFA via conditional access on your IdP. We also support SSO for both the Console and API key issuance flows with RBAC layered on top.
[01:38] Hannah: Is there an audit trail for admin actions? We need to prove who rotated keys, who started deployments, etc.
[01:44] Arjun: Yes, audit logs capture console actions, API key ops, model deployments, and role changes. Logs contain user id, timestamp, action, and resource. We can retain logs for the retention window you choose in Dedicated/Private, and for Hosted we have default retention of 90 days but enterprise plans allow extended retention.

[01:58] Priya: Can those logs be pushed to our SIEM — Splunk or Sumo?
[02:02] Arjun: Absolutely. We support log forwarding via secure syslog / HTTPS ingestion. For Private deployments, you can route logs internally so data doesn't leave your VPC.

[02:12] Liam: KMS — big one. We need to use our HSM-backed KMS (AWS KMS with custom key material or external HSM). Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed keys?
[02:21] Arjun: Yes. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or GCP KMS via a transient key for wrapping. For Dedicated/Private we can plug into your KMS/HSM via networked KMS endpoints and customer controls the master keys. We also offer an HSM integration path for FIPS/HSM-backed keys.
[02:38] Priya: Is the model shard or intermediate cache ever stored encrypted with Redwood-managed keys? We prefer customer-only master keys.
[02:45] Arjun: By default we do envelope encryption — data keys are wrapped with the customer master key when configured. For Private with customer KMS, you maintain the root material. For Hosted when you supply a CMK, we never hold the unwrapped master key. There can be transient plaintext in memory for operations, but we can document the memory handling and guardrails.

[03:02] Priya: What about KV cache and ephemeral caches — are those encrypted at rest?
[03:06] Arjun: Yes, all disk persistence is encrypted. KV cache in memory is ephemeral; if we spill to disk for any reason it's encrypted using the configured key. There's been some confusion in other notes where KV cache was transcribed as K V cash, so apologies if I keep saying it wrong.
[03:19] Maya: (laughs) we see that a lot.

[03:23] Hannah: For legal/regulatory, we need data residency. Can you pin compute to a region and prevent egress?
[03:29] Maya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can choose region and VPC controls. For Hosted we have region options and can limit routing, but Dedicated/Private is the stronger guarantee for no egress.

[03:40] Priya: Retention policy — we have both short-term logs and long-term audit archives for compliance. Do you support tiered retention?
[03:46] Arjun: We do. Logs can be kept in hot storage for 90 days by default and archived to colder storage for longer windows. With Dedicated/Private you can configure retention per log type and export to your S3 buckets with lifecycle rules.

[03:58] Priya: Is there a legal hold / ability to preserve data for investigations?
[04:02] Arjun: Yes, there's an export and hold mechanism, plus native immutability for audit snapshots when needed. We'll document the retention APIs.

[04:10] ---- 04:10 to 10:00 deep dive on KMS flow (summarized) ----
[04:12] Arjun: (walkthrough) Envelope encryption flow: Client data -> data key generated -> data encrypted -> data key wrapped with CMK -> wrapped key stored. When using customer CMK, Redwood cannot decrypt without access to customer's KMS. If you revoke access, wrapped keys become irrecoverable.
[04:36] Priya: Ok so key rotation — if we rotate CMKs we need to ensure past wrapped keys are rewrapped or accessible?
[04:42] Arjun: We recommend key rotation via new key that can decrypt old material or rewrap. We have rotation patterns we can share. If you rotate and destroy old key material without rewrapping you can lose access — that's expected with customer-managed keys.

[05:00] Liam: Network connectivity for KMS — does Redwood need direct VPC peering? How does latency look?
[05:06] Arjun: We support private endpoints (VPC endpoints) or proxying to your on-prem KMS via secure tunnels. Latency is minimal for short KMS calls but it's an extra RTT; we cache data keys locally for short periods to reduce round trips.

[05:23] Priya: RBAC — we need granular roles: who can deploy models, who can see prompts, who can export logs. How fine-grained is the RBAC?
[05:29] Arjun: RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. You can control console vs API vs model-level permissions. We also support attribute-based access controls for some enterprise plans so you can tie roles to groups coming from your IdP via SCIM.

[05:40] Priya: Can we redact PII in logs or suppress prompts in logs for certain routes?
[05:45] Arjun: We offer configurable log redaction rules — you can mask tokens or full fields. For extremely sensitive workloads we recommend Private where logs never leave your environment. For Hosted, we can mask or drop prompt content at collection time per your policy.

[05:59] Hannah: From a contract perspective, we need SLA for data availability and commitments around security incidents (notification window). What's Redwood's usual timeline?
[06:06] Maya: We commit to 72-hour incident notification for non-critical and 24-hour for critical incidents in enterprise agreements; breach notifications follow legal requirements and we can align to your need. We also have SLA options for uptime on Dedicated.

[06:20] Priya: How does Redwood handle pen tests and vulnerability reports?
[06:24] Arjun: We run regular pen tests and share summaries. For Dedicated/Private customers we can coordinate on-scope tests; we also have a responsible disclosure process and 3rd-party assessments.

[06:34] ------ Timestamps jump to specific questions ------
[07:10] Priya: A few nitty gritty items: 1) Where are model weights stored for Hosted — are they encrypted with CMK? 2) Is there an ability to lock down outbound egress from the infer nodes?
[07:21] Arjun: Model weights are stored encrypted at rest; disk encryption keys are wrapped with the cluster key and we can layer a CMK for an extra envelope. Regarding egress, in Dedicated/Private you control egress via VPC settings and egress firewall rules. Hosted has egress control features for enterprise customers but Dedicated/Private is the recommendation for strict egress requirements.

[07:40] Priya: Do you have SOC2 control mappings to ISO/PCI/GDPR?
[07:44] Maya: Yes, we maintain mappings and can provide a control matrix; that will be in the packet we send.

[08:00] Liam: We run internal audits — how long are artifacts available? For example, log snapshots for an audit that occurred six months ago.
[08:06] Arjun: Depends on your retention configuration. For Hosted default 90 days; we can extend to 1 year+ as an add-on. For Dedicated/Private you own the archive and can keep indefinitely per your storage policy.

[08:18] Priya: API keys — can we enforce expiration and rotation policies from our side?
[08:22] Maya: Yes. API keys support TTLs and can be rotated; our SCIM integration helps with provisioning and deprovisioning. You can also restrict scopes on keys.

[08:31] Hannah: For legal, any subprocessor lists and supplier attestations?
[08:35] Maya: We have an up-to-date subprocessor list we can share; it includes cloud providers and certain infra vendors. We can include supplier attestations in the pack.

[08:44] Priya: Are there features to prevent model exfiltration — like prompt telemetry or hallucination filters?
[08:50] Arjun: We have content filters and output policies, and you can route outputs through post-processing filters. Exfil prevention is mainly about controlling the model outputs and restricting integrations; it's more of architecture plus policy. We'll cover mitigation patterns.

[09:02] Priya: For Private, what's installed on-prem — agent or full control plane?
[09:06] Arjun: It's a private control plane with customer-managed networking; you run the runtime in your environment. There's an optional agent for updates and telemetry that you can opt out of for air-gapped installs.

[09:16] Maya: Quick follow-up — would you be more interested in Dedicated for staging and Private for prod, or Private across the board?
[09:23] Priya: We're leaning Dedicated for non-sensitive and Private for regulated models. Cost will be a factor though.

[09:29] Liam: One more technical — can we get a low-level diagram showing where the keys live, what calls happen on inference path, and where logs are generated and forwarded?
[09:36] Arjun: Yes, I'll draw that and include in the follow-up packet.

[09:42] ----- brief pause, cross-talk -----
[10:00] Hannah: On contracts, we may need bespoke clauses around data deletion certification and audit cooperation. Is Redwood open to that?
[10:06] Maya: Yes we do tailored contract clauses for enterprise. We'll have legal coordinate with you after we share the security pack.

[10:13] Priya: A question on data retention API — can we programmatically delete prompt logs older than X days?
[10:18] Arjun: Yes, deletion APIs exist and we also support auto-archival and retention policies at the route level. We can show the API contract.

[10:26] Priya: Anything else we should be aware of regarding compliance posture?
[10:29] Maya: For highly regulated industries, Private deployments plus customer KMS and network isolation are the most conservative route. If you need proof of non-repudiation for logs, we can add cryptographic signing for audit entries.

[10:40] Priya: Can you sign logs with a customer key?
[10:43] Arjun: We can support log signing using a customer-managed key, yes — it's a specific feature but available for enterprise projects.

[10:49] ----- 10:49 to 25:00 more granular examples and customer questions (condensed) -----
[25:05] Priya: Ok last things: 1) Data residency for EU customers — do you have dedicated EU regions? 2) Pen test coordination window?
[25:12] Maya: We have EU regions and can pin workloads. For pen tests, we require a scope and a two-week coordination window for Dedicated/Private.

[25:20] Hannah: On indemnity and liability caps — we'll go into that with legal but please note we'll seek usual enterprise protections.
[25:25] Maya: Understood.

[25:30] Liam: For the follow-up demo can we include a quick on-prem mock where we show KMS calls and disabled egress?
[25:36] Arjun: Yes — we'll set up a short tech session, maybe 60 minutes, with logs and KMS flow.

[25:44] ----- Closing (recap + next steps) -----
[25:48] Maya: Quick recap — Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts, control matrix, network diagram, KMS integration guide and Terraform snippet, and log forwarding options. Sherwood to send retention policy and list of regulated datasets. We'll schedule the infra demo with Arjun for next week.
[26:05] Priya: Sounds good. Preferred times are mornings PST.
[26:08] Maya: Great, we'll propose slots. Anything else?
[26:11] Hannah: No, that's it from legal for now.
[26:14] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[26:16] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up.
[26:18] Recording ends.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription with medium confidence; some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed.
